book.title: Hold Me Tight: Seven Conversations for a Lifetime of Love
book.author: Sue Johnson

confidence_note: Book text not read; facts from Wikipedia (EFT) and secondary pages on the demon dialogues. Omitted: invented couple scene, claimed session counts, quoted questions from old text, gender roles. DB title is 'İlişki Psikolojisi'.
facts: The book is built on seven conversations; the first is about recognising the demon dialogues.
Johnson and Les Greenberg formulated and tested Emotionally Focused Therapy in 1985; Johnson later integrated attachment theory, treated as the defining theory of adult love.
The therapy aims to reshape attachment bonds toward 'effective dependency', including secure attachment.
Johnson frames a pursuing partner's protest as an attachment protest: in effect asking whether they matter. Image: one person knocking on a brick wall hoping the other opens it.
EFT places the problem in the reinforcing cycle between partners, not in one partner; stage 1 tracks the cycle and reframes the problem as the cycle.

A 2019 meta-analysis (Beasley and Ager): EFT significantly improves relationship satisfaction, gains sustained up to two years. A 1999 meta-analysis by Johnson et al. found a larger effect than other couple interventions; James Coyne later called it poor quality.
First couples manual 1988; nine steps in three stages; anxious partners seek reassurance and may use blame, avoidant partners solve problems dispassionately (Johnson and Sims 2000).
scene_details: one person knocking on a brick wall
a loop that repeats between two people
tension: A fight about anything may be one partner asking whether they matter.
opening_idea: Open on the brick wall image or the cycle as the problem.

lessons.idea: Ask what a protest is reaching for before answering its topic.
lessons.anchor: protest as the question 'do I matter?'

reflect_final: In an argument you keep having, what is the question underneath for you?

use_cases.move: Say the question under it and ask theirs.
Say what you want: you to be there.
Ask what they hope to hear.

pocket_idea: Behind a sharp complaint often sits one question: do I matter to you.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Fights as one question asked many ways.
